provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after 'nos'; 1862 spells adjuvante, the 1962 adiuvante. Corroboration: 1604 at lines 14411-14420, 'DEus, qui nos in tantis periculis constitutos, pro humana scis fragilitate non posse subsistere...', likewise without the comma after 'nos' and supplying the initial the 1862 layer loses. Recorded limitation: The 1862 layer LOSES the opening word: line 17857 begins 'us, qui nos in tantis pe-'. The ornamental D and the small-capital E of 'Deus' are both gone from the layer, so I inferred that word's letterforms rather than read them; the 1604 line cited above prints 'DEus, qui nos' at exactly this place. Every other word here is clean apart from 'fragilitete' (17859) and 'aajuvante' (17863). Confidence is medium for that reason and no other; the verdict itself is not in doubt. All 1862 readings in this proposal rest on the tracked whole-book text layer alone. No page image of the 1862 exists locally for the temporal run and none was downloaded.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui nos, in tantis periculis constitutos, pro humana scis fragilitate
non posse subsistere: da nobis salutem mentis et corporis; ut ea, quae pro
peccatis nostris patimur, te adjuvante vincamus. Per Dominum.

It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after quaesumus; 1862 sets a comma after oblatum; the 1962 sets none; 1862 sets a comma before 'et muniat'; the 1962 sets none; 1862 spells hujus, the 1962 huius; 1862 conclusion is the short cue 'Per Dominum.' where the 1962 prints 'Per Dominum nostrum.'. Corroboration: 1604 at line 14479, 'ab omni malo purget semper, & muniat. Per Dominum'; and 1570 at lines 20871-20873, 'ab omni malo pur-get (mper c muniat. Per dnm'. Recorded limitation: THE 1862 LAYER DOES NOT READ 'purget' HERE. Line 17961 reads 'Surget semper, et miiniat.' - the initial letterform is damaged. I did not repair it silently: I read the layer as it stands, then corroborated the word at the same place in two public-domain witnesses, the 1604 at line 14479 and the 1570 at lines 20871-20873, both of which print 'purget'. The letterforms of that one word are therefore inferred and not read, and confidence is medium on that account. The layer also damages 'crineii' for 'sacrificii' (17958, with 'sa-' ending 17957), 'obliltum' for oblatum, and '>6minum' for Dominum. All 1862 readings in this proposal rest on the tracked whole-book text layer alone. No page image of the 1862 exists locally for the temporal run and none was downloaded.
